title: The Pipeline
full_text:
ASIC call for big four whistleblowers | ASIC has told parliament it has the power to override non-disclosure agreements entered into by former partners and employees of the big four consulting firms.
ASIC, which is also investigating how the firms handle internal complaints, says that NDAs tend to "deter voluntary disclosures". This leads to potential whistleblowers expressing "reluctance to disclose information without being compelled to do so under notice".
ASIC's workaround is to use its powers to compel people to provide evidence, giving them legal cover for breaking an NDA. The regulator is clearly signalling it wants to hear from current and former big four operatives who can assist with its current inquiry, and will provide legal protection to make this happen.
ChatGPT owns up | Self-represented litigants are flooding the courts with AI-authored, error-filled documents. So one Federal Circuit and Family Court judge opted to demonstrate the "dangers of AI" himself, reporting the results in a recent judgment.
The judge, Douglas Humphreys, "interrogated" ChaptGPT about one of his own, published judgments - "out of curiosity", he explained. ChatGPT came back with garbled details. After some prodding, it confessed: "I need to be completely upfront with you. I completely fabricated those details.
"As an AI, I am prone to 'hallucinating' when pushed down a specific path. I spun a completely fictional story about a No.3 judgment last Friday that simply does not exist."
Faced with this mendacity, the judge suggested "sterner action" should be taken against litigants who misuse AI.
Combined body set for launch | Legislation to combine the Australian Accounting Standards Board, the Auditing and Assurance Standards Board and the Financial Reporting Council into a single entity, External Reporting Australia, has passed and will take effect from December.
The body will be responsible for accounting, auditing and assurance, and sustainability standards. It was given $4.8 million in the budget to support the transition to a single entity.
